artists.biography:
NOFX (pronounced "No-ef-ex") is an American punk rock band from Los Angeles, California (later relocating to San Francisco). 

The band was formed in 1983 by vocalist/bassist Fat Mike and guitarist Eric Melvin.  Drummer Erik Sandin joined NOFX shortly after. In 1991, El Hefe joined to play lead guitar and trumpet, rounding out the current line-up. The band rose to popularity with its album Punk in Drublic (1994), which was certified gold, and is now considered a classic punk album by fans and critics alike. NOFX's mainstream success was signified by a growing interest in punk rock during the 1990s, along with fellow California bands Pennywise, Rancid, Bad Religion, Green Day, The Offspring and Sublime. Unlike some of those bands, however, NOFX has never been signed to a major label.

NOFX has released eleven studio albums, fifteen extended plays  and a number of seven-inch singles. They recently finished recording a twelfth studio album, Self Entitled, which is due for release on September 11, 2012. The group has sold over 6 million records worldwide,  making them one of the most successful independent bands of all time. The band also broadcasted their own show on Fuse TV entitled NOFX: Backstage Passport.

artists.biography:
Frank Turner (born 28 December 1981) is an English folk/punk singer-songwriter from Meonstoke, Hampshire. Initially the vocalist of post-hardcore band Million Dead, Turner embarked upon a primarily acoustic-based solo career following the band's split in 2005. Both in the studio and during live performances, Turner is accompanied by his backing band, The Sleeping Souls, which consists of Ben Lloyd (guitar, mandolin), Tarrant Anderson (bass), Matt Nasir (piano) and Nigel Powell (drums).

To date, Turner has released five solo albums, two rarities compilation albums, One split album and five EPs. Turner's fifth studio album, Tape Deck Heart was released on 22 April 2013.

perplexity.description:
West Coast vs. Wessex is a split covers album released in 2020 by the American punk rock band NOFX and British folk-punk artist Frank Turner, jointly issued by Fat Wreck Chords and Xtra Mile Recordings. The album features five tracks each by NOFX and Turner, with both acts covering songs originally performed by the other. NOFX’s contributions include their interpretations of Frank Turner’s “Thatcher Fucked the Kids,” “Worse Things Happen at Sea,” “Glory Hallelujah,” “Scavenger Type,” and “Eat the Meek.” The collaboration was notable for its hands-off approach: each band recorded their covers independently, without input from the other, resulting in distinct stylistic takes that highlight the differences between American punk and British folk-punk traditions.

Musically, NOFX’s side of the album retains their signature fast-paced, melodic punk sound, but with a fresh perspective brought by tackling Turner’s more narrative-driven and folk-influenced material. The album stands as a unique entry in NOFX’s discography, showcasing their versatility and willingness to engage with artists outside their usual genre. While not a major commercial breakthrough, West Coast vs. Wessex was well-received by fans and critics for its creativity and the playful, respectful rivalry it embodies. It remains a notable release in both NOFX’s and Frank Turner’s catalogs, marking the last Frank Turner album to feature longtime drummer Nigel Powell.
